newsitem.title: USA: Dollar hits 33-month high vs yen, 20-week high vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hits 33-month high vs yen, 20-week high vs mark.

text.p: The dollar rose to a 33-month high against the Japanese yen and a 20-week high against the German mark Tuesday, riding the continued strength of the British pound and a spike in oil prices, foreign exchange dealers said.
Sterling posted new highs for the third consecutive session as investors jumped in to capitalise on the rally.

"Right now, a lot of people have to buy sterling. They are getting caught at these levels; surprised at how fast it's moved up," said Mark Gargano, managing director of currency derivatives at First Union National Bank.
The pound touched a one-year high of 1.5875 against the dollar and a 44-month high of 178.00 against the yen in late U.S. trading.
A rise in sterling tends to aid the dollar as investment flows out of other currencies in Japan and Europe, dealers said.
"The start of this whole move in the dollar was the rise in sterling/mark," said Seth Garrett, chief dealer at CS First Boston.
Meanwhile, a spike to six-year highs in oil prices, coupled with increased expectations that Japan will hold domestic interest rates steady, hurt the yen.

Japanese polls show the ruling Liberal Democratic Party will likely lead the next government coalition after the Oct. 20th general election, keeping in place its present policy of delaying an increase in Japanese interest rates.
Also, Japan relies heavily on imported oil and is especially vulnerable to a rise in oil prices, which are denominated in dollars.
The dollar touched a high of 112.39 yen, up from Monday's close of 111.66, before ending at 112.25.
The dollar closed at 1.5408 marks after touching a 1.5412 mark high. it closed Monday at 1.5290 marks.
Dealers also cited pent-up demand for dollars after the U.S. currency spent the last several sessions in a very narrow trading range.
The dollar finally broke through stubborn technical resistance Tuesday, attracting considerable buying interest, they said.
U.S. stocks and bonds ended little changed on Tuesday, but the recent strength of U.S. assets continues to bolster the dollar, dealers said.
"There is still a lot of capital flowing into those markets and as long as there are no major set-backs, they will continue to help the dollar," said Gargano.
Finland's entry over the weekend into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism continued to weigh heavily on the currencies of leading European nations, dealers said.
"I think that is really what's pulling the dollar up against Europe," said Bill Bertha, chief dealer at Mellon Bank.
In other trading, the dollar closed at 1.2685 Swiss francs, up from 1.2530 at Monday's close. The dollar inched up to Canadian $1.3546 from C$1.3525.
